dating_note: Start c.275 CE = earliest dated Blemmyes activity in GHA II ch.7 (Probus 276–282). The Blemmyes=Beja equation is customary, NOT proven (GHA II ch.10); GHA II ch.11 says earlier Meroitic-era Majai/Reheres 'could have been' Beja ancestors, so earlier origins are possible. Ongoing people, not a polity.

events.en: Blemmyes (GHA II: 'customarily identified with the Bedja tribes') raid Upper Egypt; suppressed under Probus (276–282 CE)
events.ar: البليميون (تاريخ أفريقيا العام، المجلد الثاني: «يُطابَقون عادةً مع قبائل البجة») يغيرون على صعيد مصر؛ قُمعوا في عهد بروبوس (276–282 م)

events.en: After Meroe's fall the Nobades push the Blemmyes ('Bega or Buga') into the eastern desert
events.ar: بعد سقوط مروي دفع النوباديون البليميين («البجة أو البوجة») إلى الصحراء الشرقية

events.en: Nomadic Bedja of the hinterland behind the Red Sea ports; by the 14th century most were formally Islamized, and the northernmost groups (Hadariba, 'Ababda) gradually Arabized
events.ar: رعاة إبل رحّل في تلال البحر الأحمر؛ أسلمة تدريجية وتعريب متفاوت

geopolitics_en: Arab merchants 'had already started to settle in coastal towns like 'Aydhāb, Bādi' and Sawākin in the second/eighth century. The hinterland was inhabited by the turbulent nomadic Bēdja whose repeated incursions harassed Upper Egypt for a long time'; because 'the Bēdja were without any centralized political organization', Muslim treaties 'covered only a part of their groups' (GHA III ch.3 p.82). In 1571 'the Fundj (or perhaps more accurately the Bēdja) attacked Sawākin and besieged it for three months' (GHA V ch.7 p.175).
geopolitics_ar: تفصلهم تلال البحر الأحمر عن وادي النيل؛ وكانت سواكن متجهة نحو البحر الأحمر والجزيرة العربية (هولت وديلي، المقدمة ص1، 6).
culture_dominance_en: Arab immigrants 'intermarried with the Bēdja ruling families; their children became chiefs of some of the Bēdja groups' (GHA III ch.3 p.82). 'The northernmost Bēdja groups, the Hadāriba and 'Ababda, gradually became Arabized, even adopting fictitious Arab genealogies, but their ancient beliefs were only thinly disguised by Islam'; 'by the eighth/fourteenth century the majority of Bēdja were formally Islamized' (p.83).
culture_dominance_ar: أسلموا مع تعريب متفاوت يقتصر أحياناً على ادعاء نسب عربي (هولت وديلي، المقدمة ص6).
economy_en: Pastoral nomads ('the turbulent nomadic Bēdja', GHA III ch.3 p.82). Between the tenth and thirteenth centuries 'trade routes across the Bēdja country from the Nile Valley to Red Sea ports' developed (pp.82–83). No source read describes Beja herding or the modern Gash and Tokar schemes.
economy_ar: رعي الإبل؛ مع بعض الاستقرار المرتبط بمشروعات القاش وطوكر الزراعية الحديثة (هولت وديلي، المقدمة ص6).
